questions.q: A long straight wire of radius a carries a steady current I. The current is uniformly distributed across its cross section. The ratio of the magnetic field at $\frac{a}{2}$ and $2 a$ from axis of the wire is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}_1 2 \pi \frac{\mathrm{a}}{2}=\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \frac{\mathrm{I}}{4} \\ & \mathrm{~B}_1=\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{I}}{4 \pi \mathrm{a}} \\ & \mathrm{B}_2 2 \pi 2 \mathrm{a}=\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{I} \\ & \mathrm{B}_2=\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{I}}{4 \pi \mathrm{a}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
An electron is moving along the positive x-axis. If uniform magnetic field is applied parallel to the negative z-axis, then

A.The electron will experience magnetic force along positive y-axis

B.The electron will experience magnetic force along negative y-axis

C.The electron will not experience any force in magnetic field

D.The electron will continue to move along the positive x-axis

E.The electron will move along circular path in magnetic field

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The Lorentz force is given by

$\overset{→}{F} = q\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}$

$= - e\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}$

So,~$\overset{^}{F} = \overset{^}{i} \times \overset{^}{k} = - \overset{^}{j}$.

$\overset{→}{F}is\text{along} - y\text{axis}$

As the magnetic field is perpendicular to the velocity, motion would be circular.

questions.q: A wire $X$ of length $50$ cm carrying a current of $2A$ is placed parallel to a long wire $Y$ of length $5m$. The wire $Y$ carries a current of $3A$. The distance between two wires is $5$ cm and currents flow in the same direction. The force acting on the wire $Y$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
& An attractive force will act normal to& $X$~towards $Y$ because the direction of the currents in the wires is the same.

Force exerted on length~$l$ due to the magnetic field is given as~$F = {F}_{XY} = {F}_{YX} = {I}_{1}{l}_{1}{B}_{12}$

$⇒ F = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{I}_{1}{I}_{2}}{2\pir}{l}_{1}$

Given here,~${I}_{1} = 2A, {I}_{2} = 3A, {l}_{1} = 5m, r = 5cm$.

Putting the values, we have

$F = \dfrac{4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 2 \times 3}{2\pi \times 5 \times {10}^{- 2}} \times 50 \times {10}^{- 2}$

$= 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 5}N$~directed towards wire~$X$.

questions.q: An iron rod of volume ${10}^{- 3}m^{3}$ and relative permeability $1000$ is placed as core in a solenoid with$10turns{cm}^{- 1}$ . If a current of $0 . 5A$ is passed through the solenoid, then the magnetic moment of the rod will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,

Volume of iron rod is,& $V = {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$

Relative permeability,~${μ}_{r} = 1000$

No of turns per unit length of solenoid is,~$n = \dfrac{N}{l} = 10turns{cm}^{- 1} = 1000turnsm^{- 1}$

Current through the solenoid is,~$i = 0 . 5A$

Magnetic moment of an iron core solenoid is given by,

$M = ( {μ}_{r} - 1 ) NiA$

$⇒ M = \left({μ}_{r} - 1\right)Ni\dfrac{V}{l} = \left({μ}_{r} - 1\right)\dfrac{N}{l}iV$

$⇒ M = \left(1000 - 1\right) \times 1000 \times 0 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$⇒ M = 499 . 5 \approx 500Am^{2}$

questions.q: Two magnetic dipoles $X$ and $Y$ are placed at a separation $d$ , with their axes perpendicular to each other. The dipole moment of $Y$ is twice that of $X$ . A particle of charge $q$ is passing through their mid-point $P$ , at angle $\theta = {45}^{o}$ with the horizontal line, as shown in figure. What would be the magnitude of force on the particle at that instant? ( $d$ is much larger than the dimension of the dipole)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
{B}_{X} = 2\left(\dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\right)\dfrac{M}{d / 2}$ along $x$ -axis
${B}_{Y} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi} \left(2M\right)\left(d / 2\right)$ along $y$ -axis
${B}_{X} = {B}_{Y}$

Hence ${B}_{net}$ will be at ${45}^{o}$ from $x$-axis.
Now, velocity and magnetic field are in same direction. Hence no force will act on the particle.

$$$

questions.q: Magnetic fields at two points on the axis of a circular coil at a distance of $0 . 05m$ and $0 . 2m$ from the centre are in the ratio $8: 1$. The radius of coil is _______ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know, the magnetic field on the axis of a current carrying circular ring is given by

$B = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{2NIA}{\left(R^{2} + x^{2}\right)3 / 2}$

$∴ \dfrac{B1}{{B}_{2}} = \dfrac{8}{1} = \left[\dfrac{R^{2} + \left(0 . 2\right)2}{R^{2} + \left(0 . 05\right)2}\right]3 / 2$

$4 \left[R^{2} + \left($0 . 05\right)2\right] = \left[$R^{2} + \left($0 . 2\right)2\right]$

$4R^{2} - R^{2} = \left($0 . 2\right)2 - 4 $\times \left($0 . 05\right)2$

$4R^{2} - R^{2} = \left($0 . 2\right)2 - \left($0 . 1\right)2$

$3R^{2} = 0 . 3 \times0 . 1$

$R^{2} = \left($0 . 1\right)2 ⇒ R = 0 . 1$

$

questions.q: Two ions of masses $4amu$~ and $16amu$~have charges $+ 2e$ and $+ 3e$ respectively. These ions pass through the region of the constant perpendicular magnetic field. The kinetic energy of both ions is the same. Then:
options: lighter ion will be deflected less than heavier ion
lighter ion will be deflected more than heavier ion
both ions will be deflected equally
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relation between linear moment and radius in terms of the magnitude of magnetic field and charge of a particle,& $r = \dfrac{P}{qB} = \dfrac{2m{k}_{e}}{qB}$

$⇒ r ∝ \dfrac{m}{q}⇒ \dfrac{r1}{r2} = \dfrac{3}{4}⇒ {r}_{2} > {r}_{1}$.

questions.q:
A massless square loop, of wire of resistance $10Ω$,~supporting a mass of $1g$,~hangs vertically with one of its sides in a uniform magnetic field of ${10}^{3}G$, directed outwards in the shaded region. A dc~voltage $V$ is applied to the loop. For what value of $V$, the magnetic force will exactly balance the weight of the supporting mass of $1g$?

(If sides of the loop $= 10cm, g = 10ms^{- 2}$)

.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For balancing of force,&

Magnetic force& \left({F}_{m}\right) =$weight of supporting mass~\left(mg\right)$.

$∴ ILB = mg$

$∴ \left(\dfrac{V}{R}\right)LB = mg \left($∵ $\text{From Ohm's law},$I = $\dfrac{V}{R}\right)

$∴ V = $\dfrac{mgR}{LB}

=\dfrac{\left(1 \times {10}^{- 3}kg\right)\left(10ms^{- 2}\right)\left(10Ω\right)}{\left(0 . 1m\right)\left({10}^{3} \times {10}^{- 4}T\right)} =$10V$

$

questions.q:
Given below two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Non-polar materials do not have any permanent dipole moment.

Reason (R): When a non-polar material is placed in an electric field, the centre of the positive charge distribution of it's individual atom or molecule coincides with the centre of the negative charge distribution.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A)& and (R)& are correct and (R)& is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Non-polar materials do not have any permanent dipole moment. This statement is true.

When a non-polar material is placed in an electric field, centre of positive charge is pushed in the direction of the electric field and centre of the negative charge is pushed in the direction opposite to the electric field. Hence, they don't coincide. Therefore, reason is false.

questions.q: A charged particle going around in a circle can be considered to be a current loop. A particle of a mass& $m$~carrying charge~$q$~is moving in a plane with speed~$v$~under the influence of magnetic field~$\overset{→}{B}$. The magnetic moment of this moving particle is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$i = \dfrac{q}{T} = \dfrac{qv}{2\pir}$

$M = i \times \pir^{2}$

$= \dfrac{2v}{2\pir} \times \pir^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}qv \times \dfrac{mv}{qB}$

Direction of $\overset{→}{M}$ is opposite of $\overset{→}{B}$ therefore

$\overset{→}{M} = \dfrac{- {mv}^{2}\overset{→}{B}}{2B^{2}}$

A circular conducting coil of radius $2R$ is placed in the equitorial plane of the solenoid and concentric with the solenoid. The current induced in the outer coil is correctly depicted, as a function of time, by:$

questions.solution:
${ϕ}_{outer} = \left({\mu}_{0}nKte^{- \alphat}\right)4\piR^{2}$
$ε = \dfrac{- dϕ}{dt} = - {μ}_{0}nK4\piR^{2} ( e^{- \alphat}\left[1 - \alphat\right] )$
${i}_{induced} = \dfrac{- ce^{- \alphat}\left[1 - \alphat\right]}{Resistance}$
At $t = 0,{I}_{induced} = - ve$
From the above equation and initial value of current we can say the correct graph is B.

In a moving coil galvanometer, two moving coils $M_1$ and $M_2$ have the following particulars :
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{R}_1=5 \Omega, \mathrm{~N}_1=15, \mathrm{~A}_1=3.6 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2, \mathrm{~B}_1=0.25 \mathrm{~T} \\ & \mathrm{R}_2=7 \Omega, \mathrm{~N}_2=21, \mathrm{~A}_2=1.8 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2, \mathrm{~B}_2=0.50 \mathrm{~T}
\end{aligned}$
Assuming that torsional constant of the springs are same for both coils, what will be the ratio of voltage sensitivity of $M_1$ and $M_2$ ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Voltage sensitivity }=\frac{\theta}{V}=\frac{N A B}{c R} \\ & \text { Ratio }==\left(\frac{\mathrm{N}_1 \mathrm{~A}_1 \mathrm{~B}_1}{\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{~A}_2 \mathrm{~B}_2}\right) \frac{\mathrm{R}_2}{\mathrm{R}_1}=\frac{15 \times 3.6 \times 0.25}{21 \times 1.8 \times 0.5} \times \frac{7}{5}=\frac{1}{1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A charge particle moving in magnetic field $B,$ has the components of velocity along $B$ as well as perpendicular to $B$. The path of the charge particle will be
options: helical path with the axis perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field $B$
helical path with the axis along magnetic field $B$
straight along the direction of magnetic field $B$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the radius of the path followed by the charged particle under an external magnetic field can be written as

$r = \dfrac{mv}{Bq} . . . \left(1\right)

The perpendicular component of velocity results in circular motion, while the& parallel component results in linear motion. Hence, the path of the charged particle is helical in nature, the axis of which lies along the direction of the magnetic field.

$

questions.q: A magnetic dipole experiences a torque of $80 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~m}$ when placed in uniform magnetic field in such a way that dipole moment makes angle of $60^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ with magnetic field. The potential energy of the dipole is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\tau=\mathrm{M} \times $\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{MB}$ \sin 60=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \mathrm{MB}=80 \sqrt{3}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{MB}=160 \\ & \mathrm{U}=-\mathrm{M} \cdot \mathrm{B}=-\mathrm{MB} \cos 60 \\ & \mathrm{U}=-160 \times 1 / 2=-80 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two concentric circular loops of radii ${r}_{1} = 30cm$ and ${r}_{2} = 50cm$ are placed in $X - Y$ plane as shown in the figure. A current $I = 7A$ is flowing through them in the direction as shown in figure. The net magnetic moment of this system of two circular loops is approximately
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net magnetic moment of the system is&

$\overset{→}{M} = - I{A}_{1}\overset{^}{k} + I{A}_{2}\overset{^}{k}$~ ~ (Here currents in both circular loops are in opposite direction)

$\overset{→}{M} = - I\pi\left(0 . 5\right)2\overset{^}{k} + I\pi\left(0 . 3\right)2\overset{^}{k}$~ ~

$\overset{→}{M} = - 7 \times \dfrac{22}{7}\left(\dfrac{25}{100} - \dfrac{9}{100}\right)\overset{^}{k}= - 22\left(\dfrac{16}{100}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

~$\overset{→}{M} = - 3 . 52\overset{^}{k}Am^{2}$

$= - \dfrac{7}{2}\overset{^}{k}Am^{2}$

questions.q: A long, straight Wire of radius a carries a current distributed uniformly over its cross-section. The ratio of the magnetic fields due to the wire at distance $\dfrac{a}{3}$ and $2a$ , respectively from the axis of the wire is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${B}_{A} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}ir}{2\pia^{2}} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i\dfrac{a}{3}}{2\pia^{2}} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{\pia^{2}}\dfrac{a}{6} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{6\pia}$
${B}_{B} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2\pi\left(2a\right)}$
$\dfrac{{B}_{A}}{{B}_{B}} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.q: A circular coil having $N$ turns and radius $r$ carries a current $I .$ It is held in the $XZ$ plane in a magnetic field $B\overset{^}{i}$ . The torque on the coil due to the magnetic field is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic moment \left(\overset{→}{M}\right) = NI\left(\pir^{2}\right)\overset{^}{j}$
Torque \left(\overset{→}{τ}\right) = \overset{→}{M} \times \overset{→}{B}$
$= \left(NI\left(\pir^{2}\right)\overset{^}{j}\right) \times ( B\overset{^}{i} )$
$= BNI\pir^{2} ( - \overset{^}{k} ) Nm$
\left|\overset{→}{τ}\right| = BNI\pir^{2}Nm$

$

questions.q: An electron in a hydrogen atom revolves around its nucleus with a speed of $6 . 76 \times {10}^{6}ms^{– 1}$ in an orbit of radius $0 . 52Å$. The magnetic field produced at the nucleus of the hydrogen atom is _______ $T$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnetic field due to the electron is given by&

$B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}qvsin90 °}{4\pir^{2}}$

The given data is~

$v = 6 . 76 \times {10}^{6}ms^{- 1}r = 0 . 52 \times {10}^{- 10}m$

Thus, the magnetic field is~

$B = \dfrac{{10}^{- 7} \times \left(1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}\right) \times \left(6 . 76 \times {10}^{6}\right)}{0 . 52 \times 0 . 52 \times {10}^{- 20}} = 40T$

questions.q: A wire of length $314$ cm carrying current of $14A$ is bent to form a circle. The magnetic moment of the coil is $A - m^{2}$. [Given $\pi = 3 . 14$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Length of the wire& $l$~when bent~becomes circumference~of the loop, whose radius is given by~$R = \dfrac{l}{2\pi} = \dfrac{314}{100\left(2 \times 3 . 14\right)} = \dfrac{1}{2}m$

Magnetic moment of the coil is~$M = IA$

$= 14 \times \piR^{2}$

$= 14 \times \left(3 . 14\right) \times \dfrac{1}{4}$

$= 10 . 99 \approx 11 . 00A - m^{2}$
